title: Bolo de mel
subtitle: The dense, spiced Madeiran molasses cake that keeps for months
excerpt: Bolo de mel is the traditional Christmas cake of Madeira, made with molasses, spices, dried fruit, and nuts. It is baked months before Christmas and improves significantly with age; a well-made bolo de mel is still good after a year. The flavour is complex and deep, darker and more intense than a British Christmas cake.
sourceNotes: Bolo de mel (literally honey cake, though it uses molasses) is the defining traditional cake of Madeira, consumed at Christmas and throughout the year. The recipe has been consistent for centuries, documented in Madeiran culinary heritage publications. The combination of molasses, cinnamon, cloves, anise, and dried fruit with walnuts and almonds is the canonical form.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bolo de mel is traditionally made weeks or months before eating. Wrap tightly in baking paper and store in an airtight tin at room temperature. The spiced molasses flavour deepens significantly over time.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 160 degrees Celsius. Fan oven: 145 degrees Celsius. Low and slow. The dense batter can burn on the outside before the centre is done if baked too hot.

glossaryTerms.definition: Bolo de mel improves with age. The molasses continues to develop flavour and the texture softens over weeks. Traditionally baked for Christmas in October or November. Wrapped tightly and stored in a cool, dry place, a bolo de mel keeps for 6 to 12 months.

content.text: Bolo de mel is built on molasses, which is what gives it the deep, almost liquorice-tinged flavour. The

quality comes from the sugar concentration in the molasses. Make it at least two weeks before eating; a month is better. The spice blend is traditionally cinnamon, cloves, and anise; fennel seeds can stand in for anise.
Preheat the oven to 160 degrees Celsius. Grease and line a 23 cm round cake tin with a double layer of baking paper on the base and sides.
Melt the butter and molasses together in a saucepan over low heat, stirring until combined. Remove from heat and stir in the sugar. Leave to cool until lukewarm.

Beat the eggs into the cooled molasses mixture one at a time. Add the rum if using. Sift in the flour, baking powder, and spices and fold until combined. Stir in the raisins, walnuts, flaked almonds, and mixed peel.

Pour into the tin and bake for 55 to 65 minutes. The cake is done when a skewer inserted in the centre comes out with only a few sticky crumbs. The top will look very dark; this is correct. Cool completely in the tin.

The dark colour of molasses makes it impossible to judge doneness by eye. Use a skewer: a clean skewer with no wet batter means it is done. The cake feels firm on top when pressed gently. If the skewer is wet, add 10 minutes and test again.
